# Foundry

> Build reliable, observable, and testable AI agent systems in .NET

Author: Nick Cosentino (https://www.devleader.ca).

- [Home](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/) -- Build reliable .NET AI agents with generated discovery, workflows, observability, evaluation, and deterministic testing.
- [Getting Started](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/getting-started/) -- Build Foundry, choose the packages for your scenario, register the runtime, and create your first generated agent.
- [Configuration](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/configuration/) -- Understand Foundry's configuration surfaces for agents, workflows, diagnostics, evaluation, providers, and optional Needlr integration.
- [Building from Source](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/building/) -- Build, test, pack, and validate the Foundry repository from source.

## Guides

- [Overview](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/guides/) -- Choose a Foundry guide for orchestration, observability, evaluation, testing, or provider integration.

## Agent Framework

- [Integrations and Workflows](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/ai-integrations/) -- Build AI agent systems with Foundry in .NET using generated discovery, workflow orchestration, and optional Needlr integration.
- [MAF Harness](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/maf-harness/) -- Choose and configure Foundry's Microsoft Agent Framework Harness paths, generated tools, progress, defaults, and AOT profile.
- [Agent Functions](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/agent-functions/) -- Parameter optionality, default-value resolution, and DTO null-handling semantics for [AgentFunction]-decorated tools in Foundry's source-generated AIFunction wrappers.
- [Iterative Agent Loop](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/iterative-agent-loop/) -- Run workspace-driven agent iterations with bounded conversation growth and choose between iterative, Harness bundle, and hybrid context strategies.
- [Declarative Workflows](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/declarative-workflows/) -- Declarative Workflows. Foundry can run Microsoft Agent Framework declarative workflows — orchestration authored in YAML rather than code — against agents your application already owns.
- [Checkpointed Workflows](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/checkpointed-workflows/) -- Resume Microsoft Agent Framework workflows from caller-owned checkpoints without adding a second Foundry persistence model.
- [Fixed-Macro Autonomous Phases](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/autonomous-phase-pipeline/) -- Build fixed macro workflows whose Harness phases remain autonomous while deterministic artifact gates own correctness.
- [Workspace](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/workspace/) -- Workspace. IWorkspace is Foundry's file-storage abstraction for AI agent tools. It models a logical, rooted key/value store of files — agents read and write paths through this interface without caring whether the backing store is...
- [Progress Reporting](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/progress-reporting/) -- Track agent and workflow execution in real-time with Foundry's progress reporting system -- optional Needlr discovery, per-orchestration isolation, and ambient async context.
- [Pipeline Metrics](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/pipeline-metrics/) -- Pipeline-shape OpenTelemetry metrics and distributed-tracing spans emitted automatically by SequentialPipelineRunner — per-pipeline outcome, per-stage duration / tokens / tool-failures, parent + child activity spans.
- [GenAI Token Metrics](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/gen-ai-token-metrics/) -- Emit cache_read and reasoning measurements on the OpenTelemetry gen_ai.client.token.usage histogram so dashboards can answer "what's my prompt-cache hit ratio?" and "how many tokens went to reasoning vs final completion?" per LLM call.
- [Stage Termination](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/stage-termination/) -- Typed-case StageTermination hierarchy describes why a pipeline stage stopped — pattern-match in C#, low-cardinality OTel tags via ToTagValue, polymorphic JSON wire format.
- [Tool Result Middleware](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/tool-result-middleware/) -- How Foundry's ToolResultFunctionMiddleware translates tool exceptions and IToolResult returns into LLM-safe responses, and the trade-offs of enabling it.
- [Tiered Provider Selection](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/tiered-provider-selector/) -- Configure how TieredProviderSelector reacts to provider exceptions — match exception kinds, skip failing providers for a duration, run a callback on hit. Replaces the hardcoded ProviderUnavailableException catch with declarative, per-instance policies.

## Evaluation

- [Evaluation](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/evaluation/) -- Evaluation. Foundry's agent framework plugs directly into Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation without adapters or flattening.
- [Experiment Runner](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/experiment-runner/) -- Experiment Runner. Run finite evaluation cases and repeated trials with bounded concurrency, delayed retries, per-trial provider scopes, run-level measurement, structured quality policies, and deterministic JSON—without coupling the...
- [Langfuse](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/langfuse/) -- Langfuse. Send Foundry agent telemetry and Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation scores to Langfuse so agent runs and evals show up on the Langfuse dashboard — with a single call.

## Providers

- [GitHub Copilot](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/copilot/) -- Use GitHub Copilot as a direct IChatClient provider and choose between Foundry's HTTP client and Microsoft's CLI-backed AIAgent.

## Testing

- [Testing Tools](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/testing-tools/) -- Paved-path testing for [AgentFunction]-decorated tools. Use ToolInvocationRunner to exercise the source-generated AIFunction wrapper with seeded workspace state, zero hand-rolled DI, and the same code path FunctionInvokingChatClient takes in production.

## Analyzers

- [Overview](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/) -- Analyzers Overview. NexusLabs.Foundry.MicrosoftAgentFramework.Analyzers validates agent and workflow declarations at compile time. Diagnostic IDs use the FDRYMAF prefix.
- [FDRYMAF001](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF001/) -- FDRYMAF001. A type referenced in [AgentHandoffsTo(typeof(X))] is not decorated with [FoundryAgent].
- [FDRYMAF002](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF002/) -- FDRYMAF002. A group chat named "X" has only one class decorated with [AgentGroupChatMember("X")] in the compilation.
- [FDRYMAF003](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF003/) -- FDRYMAF003. A class bearing [AgentHandoffsTo] is not itself decorated with [FoundryAgent].
- [FDRYMAF004](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF004/) -- FDRYMAF004. The [AgentHandoffsTo] declarations in the compilation form a cycle (e.g. A → B → A, or A → B → C → A).
- [FDRYMAF005](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF005/) -- FDRYMAF005. An agent declares FunctionGroups = new[] { "xyz" } but no class in the compilation is decorated with [AgentFunctionGroup("xyz")].
- [FDRYMAF006](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF006/) -- FDRYMAF006. Two or more agents in the same sequential pipeline share the same Order value in their [AgentSequenceMember] attribute.
- [FDRYMAF007](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF007/) -- FDRYMAF007. The Order values declared for a sequential pipeline are non-consecutive (e.g. 1, 2, 4 — missing 3).
- [FDRYMAF008](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF008/) -- FDRYMAF008. A class decorated with [FoundryAgent] does not appear in any handoff chain, group chat, or sequential pipeline.
- [FDRYMAF009](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF009/) -- FDRYMAF009. A class bearing [WorkflowRunTerminationCondition] is not decorated with any topology attribute ([AgentHandoffsTo], [AgentGroupChatMember], or [AgentSequenceMember]).
- [FDRYMAF010](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF010/) -- FDRYMAF010. The type referenced in [AgentTerminationCondition(typeof(X))] or [WorkflowRunTerminationCondition(typeof(X))] does not implement IWorkflowTerminationCondition.
- [FDRYMAF011](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF011/) -- FDRYMAF011. A class decorated with [AgentGroupChatMember] also declares [WorkflowRunTerminationCondition].
- [FDRYMAF012](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF012/) -- FDRYMAF012. A method decorated with [AgentFunction] does not have a [System.ComponentModel.Description] attribute.
- [FDRYMAF013](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF013/) -- FDRYMAF013. A parameter on an [AgentFunction] method does not have a [System.ComponentModel.Description] attribute. CancellationToken parameters are exempt.
- [FDRYMAF014](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF014/) -- FDRYMAF014. A type listed in FoundryAgentAttribute.FunctionTypes contains no methods decorated with [AgentFunction].
- [FDRYMAF015](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF015/) -- FDRYMAF015. Code calls .ToString() on a tool result property such as ToolCallResult.Result or FunctionResultContent.Result.
- [FDRYMAF016](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF016/) -- FDRYMAF016. A named agent graph declared via [AgentGraphEdge] attributes contains a cycle.
- [FDRYMAF017](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF017/) -- FDRYMAF017. A named agent graph has [AgentGraphEdge] declarations but no [AgentGraphEntry] to identify the starting agent.
- [FDRYMAF018](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF018/) -- FDRYMAF018. A named agent graph has more than one [AgentGraphEntry] declaration.
- [FDRYMAF019](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF019/) -- FDRYMAF019. An [AgentGraphEdge] references a target type that is not decorated with [FoundryAgent].
- [FDRYMAF020](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF020/) -- FDRYMAF020. A class has [AgentGraphEdge] but is not itself decorated with [FoundryAgent].
- [FDRYMAF021](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF021/) -- FDRYMAF021. A class has [AgentGraphEntry] but is not itself decorated with [FoundryAgent].
- [FDRYMAF022](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF022/) -- FDRYMAF022. An agent that declares [AgentGraphEdge] for a named graph is not reachable from that graph's [AgentGraphEntry] point via any path.
- [FDRYMAF024](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF024/) -- FDRYMAF024. A fan-out node (a node with multiple outgoing edges) has all edges marked as IsRequired = false.
- [FDRYMAF025](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF025/) -- FDRYMAF025. Code calls CreateGraphWorkflow("graphName") on a graph that declares [AgentGraphNode(JoinMode = GraphJoinMode.WaitAny)] on one or more nodes.
- [FDRYMAF027](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF027/) -- FDRYMAF027. A node marked with [AgentGraphNode(IsTerminal = true)] also has outgoing [AgentGraphEdge] declarations.
- [FDRYMAF028](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF028/) -- FDRYMAF028. The Condition property on [AgentGraphEdge] references a method name that does not exist on the declaring class, is not static, does not return bool, or does not accept a single object? parameter.
- [FDRYMAF029](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF029/) -- FDRYMAF029. The ReducerMethod property on [AgentGraphReducer] references a method name that does not exist on the declaring class, is not static, does not return string, or does not accept IReadOnlyList<string>.
- [FDRYMAF030](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF030/) -- FDRYMAF030. An [AgentFunction] parameter is typed as string and EITHER:
- [FDRYMAF031](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF031/) -- FDRYMAF031. Two or more classes decorated with [FoundryAgent] resolve to the same published name.
- [FDRYMAF032](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF032/) -- FDRYMAF032. An [AIFunctionName] or [AIParameterName] applied to an [AgentFunction] declares a null, empty, or whitespace-only name.
- [FDRYMAF033](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/analyzers/FDRYMAF033/) -- FDRYMAF033. Either:

## Operations

- [Agent Guidance](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/agent-guidance/) -- Understand where Foundry's agent guidance lives, how it is validated, and which source owns each kind of rule.
- [GitHub-Hosted CI Runners](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/github-hosted-runners/) -- Understand Foundry's standard GitHub-hosted runner and public-repository billing boundary.
- [Documentation Publishing](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/publishing/) -- Documentation Publishing. Foundry documentation is built with MkDocs and published to a dedicated Cloudflare Pages project. The public URL is routed through the existing Dev Leader project-documentation Worker:
- [Releasing](https://www.devleader.ca/projects/foundry/releasing/) -- Releasing. Foundry releases are tag-driven and publish all production NexusLabs.Foundry.* packages together.
